title: Identify whether a paid catalyst write changes subsequent fresh-feed processing and yields useful isolated product under a reproducible common read/reset operation.

statement.current_best: Acquired Wang Chem2026 article/SI reports continuous selective acetylene removal; 200-hour stability at2sccm and100sccm two-cell purification are distinct regimes. Generic carbon-isotope/SSITKA attribution is established. Closer Lim/Hulsey/Yan2021 primary prior art covers brief pulse sweeping; comparative capability remains untested.
statement.limitation: Optimum-waveform work, raw chromatograms, complete fresh-cohort fate and calibrated common-regime exposure remain unavailable. Electronic and hidden-H/transport mechanisms are not distinguished. Cycle averages do not bound single-pulse response or conditioning/washout horizon.
statement.problem: Identify whether a paid catalyst write changes subsequent fresh-feed processing and yields useful isolated product under a reproducible common read/reset operation.
statement.proposed_mechanism: Acquire randomized isolated and periodically conditioned interventions, measured withdrawal/recovery horizons, common actual exposure and complete fresh-carbon fate. No microscopic carrier is assumed.

target.comparator: Same feed/output specification and full solvent, energy, reset and lifetime boundary against static/dynamic catalyst and acquired continuous electrochemical incumbents.
target.conditions: Same specimen/feed/exposure and waveform; complete tag/fate and missing-product bounds; target numerical acceptance threshold frozen before new measurement.
target.metric: lower simultaneous-error bound on changed fresh-cohort chemical fate and retained useful product per fully paid restored operation
target.unit: moles and product purity/recovery, plus joules and resources per isolated useful product
